steps.note: The same ~50-person company, but most business apps have moved to SaaS: only the ERP stays on-prem. HR, Sales CRM and Finance are cloud services signed into with Entra ID.
One internet connection: the ISP router hands off to a single firewall. The office, remote VPN users and suppliers all come through here.
The firewall also terminates the VPNs: always-on VPN for remote laptops (now mainly needed for the ERP) and a supplier VPN for the MSP. Both require MFA.
The firewall's management interface is only reachable from the management VLAN — two admin PAWs. Admin access from the WAN or user VLAN is switched off.
Inside: a core switch and three PoE access switches serve ~40 laptops (mostly on Wi-Fi), 8 desktops and 2 printers on the user VLAN.
On-prem identity is still the root of trust: two domain controllers (AD DS) and an enterprise CA (AD CS). These are the Tier 0 crown jewels.
Entra hybrid mode: Entra Connect syncs users from AD to Entra ID with password hash sync. Conditional Access and MFA protect every cloud sign-in.
Microsoft 365 carries day-to-day work: Exchange Online mail, Teams, SharePoint Online and OneDrive — all reached over HTTPS from wherever staff are.
HR, Sales CRM and Finance are SaaS. Staff reach them directly over HTTPS; Entra ID is the identity provider — single sign-on plus SCIM so joiners and leavers are provisioned automatically.
That makes Entra ID (and the on-prem AD it syncs from) the key to every business app. A compromised AD account now opens HR, CRM and Finance too.
The ERP stays on-prem as a VM on the Hyper-V hosts, with its database on SQL Server and nightly backups. Finance exchanges journals and invoices with it via an API integration.
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint runs on every laptop, desktop and server and streams EDR telemetry to the Defender portal.
IT is outsourced to an MSP: service desk, patching, backups, firewall changes and M365 / Defender / SaaS admin — through the supplier VPN with MFA, time-boxed and logged.
The public website is run by a third-party hosting provider, completely separate from the office network. Customers reach it directly over HTTPS.
Outside the walls: hybrid staff on home broadband, phones managed with Intune, and suppliers — Microsoft runs the tenant, the ERP vendor supports the ERP, and the payroll bureau takes the HR export.
